mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo moving average AND CPIAUCSL > 12mo moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12mo moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, which signals weak wage growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals a prolonged economic stagnation, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.
